ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, objects A and B are placed on horizontal ground, and the coefficient of kinetic friction with the ground is $\mu$ for both. Objects A and B are connected by a light string passing over a movable pulley. Now the pulley is lifted upward with a gradually increasing force. At a certain moment, the angle between the string pulling object A and the horizontal plane is $53^{\circ}$, and the angle between the string pulling object B and the horizontal plane is $37^{\circ}$. At this time, the two objects A and B are just in equilibrium. Then the mass ratio of the two objects A and B is (take the maximum static friction force to be equal to the sliding friction force, $\sin37^\circ=0.6$, $\cos37^\circ=0.8$)(　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, objects A and B are placed on horizontal ground, and the coefficient of kinetic friction with the ground is $\mu$ for both. Objects A and B are connected by a light string passing over a movable pulley. Now the pulley is lifted upward with a gradually increasing force. At a certain moment, the angle between the string pulling object A and the horizontal plane is $53^{\circ}$, and the angle between the string pulling object B and the horizontal plane is $37^{\circ}$. At this time, the two objects A and B are just in equilibrium. It is known that the maximum static friction force is taken to be equal to the sliding friction force, and $\sin37^\circ=0.6$, $\cos37^\circ=0.8$. Find the mass ratio of the two objects A and B.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, object A is on the left side and object B is on the right side, and both are placed on horizontal ground; a light string is respectively connected to A and B and passes over the pulley above, and the pulley is subjected to an upward lifting force. The string segment connected to A is inclined upward to the right, and the angle with the horizontal plane is marked as 53°; the string segment connected to B is inclined upward to the left, and the angle with the horizontal plane is marked as 37°. Reasoning: Let the tension in the string be T. When A is just in equilibrium, the horizontal component of the force of the string on A is Tcos53°, and the vertical upward component is Tsin53°. In the vertical direction, there is N_A+Tsin53°=m_A g, so N_A=m_A g-Tsin53°. In the horizontal direction, the maximum static friction force balances the horizontal component of the string: Tcos53°=μN_A=μ(m_A g-Tsin53°). Solving gives m_A g=T(cos53°/μ+sin53°). Similarly, when B is just in equilibrium, N_B+Tsin37°=m_B g, and in the horizontal direction Tcos37°=μN_B=μ(m_B g-Tsin37°). Solving gives m_B g=T(cos37°/μ+sin37°). From sin37°=0.6 and cos37°=0.8, we can obtain cos53°=0.6 and sin53°=0.8. Thus m_A g=T(0.6/μ+0.8)=T(3+4μ)/(5μ), and m_B g=T(0.8/μ+0.6)=T(4+3μ)/(5μ). Therefore, the mass ratio of A and B is m_A/m_B=(3+4μ)/(4+3μ)=(4μ+3)/(3μ+4).
